about: Bookmark sites on the latitude/longitude grid of the maps. PaleoDEM maps are in PALEOMAP paleo-coordinates (continents where they were, e.g. North America about 30 degrees east of today at 90 Ma), so a site names a place on the old globe, not a modern place. Hand-entered after checking the maps; tests re-check them.

sites.source: PaleoDEM 250 Ma: land in every direction for 3 cells (interior Pangaea, about 3450 km from the sea); open South Atlantic today

PaleoDEM 90 Ma (paleo-coordinates): shallow sea in a channel about 10 cells wide with land within 6 cells to the west (Laramidia) and the east (Appalachia): the Western Interior Seaway, centred south of the mid-latitude storm-track clouds; land on the 70 Ma map
Laurentide ice dome over Hudson Bay at the Last Glacial Maximum (hand-entered margins, src/modules/paleo/data/lgm-ice.json); global sea level about -121 m (Bintanja & van de Wal 2008)
Late Cretaceous Laramidia/Appalachia region on the PaleoDEM 65-70 Ma maps; the Sun is setting, to show day and night still turn in deep time
